julie (DevEx): Heads-up: noticed a weird SSE resume edge-case in the sample-app demo. After an auth refresh + reconnect, the client sometimes gets token-chunks out of order and the UI shows garbled partial tokens. Repro is fairly small, posting logs below.

julie (DevEx): raw stream snippet from the client when reconnecting:
```
event: token
id: 42
data: {"chunk_index":2,"payload":"AAA"}

event: token
id: 43
data: {"chunk_index":3,"payload":"BBB"}

# reconnect happens here (auth refresh)
# server resends cached chunks

event: token
id: 41
data: {"chunk_index":1,"payload":"..."}

event: token
id: 44
data: {"chunk_index":4,"payload":"CCC"}
```

julie (DevEx): The client ended up rendering 2,3,1,4. We expect to apply chunks by chunk_index, but also need to be tolerant of missing chunks when resuming.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Thanks — can you paste the reconnect headers? specifically are we using last-event-id or a custom resume token?

julie (DevEx): In the repro I used `Last-Event-ID: 43` on reconnect (browser fetch). Server also emits a `X-Resume-Token` in the payload for dedicated resume but our hosted fallback path only uses last-event-id.

lin (qa): I can reproduce in CI flaky tests. Quick note: python sdk parser currently treats consecutive `\n\n` as a boundary and accepts events in arrival order; js-sdk has an additional safety where it coalesces chunks by `id` and prefers the highest seq it saw — but that only works if id strictly increases. If server can resend older id after reconnect, js-sdk will drop it (good) but python accepts it (bad).

mike (eng-ml): Sounds like two separate issues: 1) server resend semantics (is resend supposed to deliver older ids?) and 2) client-side acceptance rules. If server replays cached fragments, it should mark them with a resume token or a monotonic stream seq. Do we have a guarantee today?

julie (DevEx): No definite guarantee for hosted fallback. Dedicated has stronger resume tokens. That mismatch is likely the root cause.

sanjay (eng-runtime): We should add a defensive client rule: accept only events with `id >= last_applied_id` and ignore duplicates/older ids. But careful: `id` might be opaque. Alternative: include a numeric `chunk_index` in data for ordering.

mike (eng-ml): We already include chunk_index in payload for long responses (streamed generation). So client can use that. But parsing library should not reorder events arbitrarily based on arrival time — it should buffer short reorders and apply by chunk_index when present.

lin (qa): Proposed quick fix in sample apps: 1) JS + Python SDKs: if payload contains `chunk_index`, apply monotonic check and drop older ones. 2) Add an integration test that simulates server replaying cached events out-of-order. I can add the test matrix.

julie (DevEx): I'll open a sample-app PR with a minimal repro harness and link the CI test. Also adding a note to onboarding docs about difference between hosted vs dedicated resume semantics.

sanjay (eng-runtime): I dug into server logs for the repro and see the server sent a replay due to a bug in the fallback routing: it forwarded cached fragments from a previous connection pool without updating the resume token. Patch idea: attach `X-Resume-Source: <conn-id>` and suppress replays unless resume token matches.

ops-jenkins: dev-external-tests/sample-apps#542 queued — running flaky-run with injected replay: true.

devex-bot: CI flakiness tracker: sample-apps/resume-tests shows 7/100 flakes this week. Linking historical ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INFR-2331

mike (eng-ml): Also callout for SDK parity: JS currently exposes a `onReorder` hook in the stream API; python does not. Let's add a `reorder_policy` param to python client (default: drop older chunks).

julie (DevEx): Sounds good. Action items: 
- sanjay: runtime fallback patch to stop stale replays (small change)
- lin: integration test simulating replay/out-of-order
- mike: python SDK reorder_policy + unit tests
- julie: sample-app repro + doc note + link to CI

julie (DevEx): @sanjay can you estimate ETA on the runtime patch? Even just a quick guard would reduce user impact. :pray:

sanjay (eng-runtime): I can have a small guard up by EOD tomorrow (fast rollbackable). Will open PR and include logs/bench notes.

lin (qa): I'll start the flaky test and add the `reorder` scenarios to the nightly matrix.

julie (DevEx): Thanks all — I'll follow up with the PR links and update the onboarding checklist. :+1:
